signals.entity: ECB — digital euro scheme rulebook v0.91, Annex D1 #4 (Acceptance device)
signals.country: Euro area — GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, AT, BG
signals.signal: The acceptance-device implementation specification carries a full ATM section (§7): manual FUNDING of a digital euro account by cash deposit at an ATM, manual DEFUNDING by cash withdrawal, and digital euro balance/transaction-history enquiry at the ATM — each specified for BOTH card-initiated and QR-code-initiated flows, with the ATM required to validate digital euro card data, trigger card authentication, request the account balance and generate a funding request to the acquirer. The document states verbatim: 'There has been no revision or modification on the ATM requirements written some months ago. ATM use cases are deprioritised and will be addressed at a later stage.' Offline digital euro holdings at the ATM are explicitly out of scope of this document. ATMs are formally classed as a 'proximity environment' acceptance device alongside POS, with a separate 'ATM Operator domain' in the architecture. NOTE: no version after v0.91 exists as at 27/08/2026; sections 8, 9 and Annex F1 remain placeholders to be written in H2-2026.
signals.source_name: ECB, Draft Digital Euro Scheme Rulebook v0.91 – Annex D1 – Front-end implementation specifications #4 Acceptance device (PDF, text extracted locally with pdfminer)
signals.implies: Directly scopes a future NCR ATM / x-core multivendor software work package for Printec: digital euro cash-in (deposit-to-wallet) and cash-out (wallet-to-cash) at the ATM, card and QR initiation, plus a new balance/statement screen — i.e. an ATM application + EMV kernel + QR reader change on every deposit/recycling machine in the euro-area footprint (Alpha Bank, Bank of Cyprus, Erste Croatia, and the AT/SI/SK/BG estates). CRITICAL COMMERCIAL POINT: because the ECB has DEPRIORITISED ATM use cases, there is no ATM deadline and no 2026-27 CAPEX trigger. Printec should position this as roadmap/discovery work (x-core readiness assessment, QR-capable fascia planning) and must NOT let banks be sold digital-euro ATM hardware on a false deadline. Budget commitment is NOT yet due; the earliest plausible commit window follows a G5 output plus a political agreement, i.e. not before H2-2027.
signals.likelihood: High that the ATM spec stays frozen through the 6-12 month horizon; low that any ATM certification obligation crystallises before the Regulation is adopted
signals.followup: Re-check Annex D1 #4 at each new rulebook version (next expected once sections 8/9/F1 are filled, H2-2026) for any change to the 'deprioritised' wording; that single sentence flipping is the buy signal for the whole footprint ATM estate.

signals.entity: ECB — RDG workstream G5 (implementation specifications for ATM and terminal providers)
signals.country: Euro area — GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, AT, BG
signals.signal: G5's mandate is now published in full. Scope: (i) initiation factors for digital euro payments at ATMs and payment terminals (NFC, QR-code); (ii) assessing NEXO as a candidate reference implementation for enabling digital euro payments at ATMs and potentially at payment terminals; (iii) assessing integration and deployment of OFFLINE digital euro functionality into the EXISTING CERTIFIED POS and ATM infrastructure; (iv) assessing security standards in the field of POS and ATM; (v) implementation specifications and standards for softPOS and mPOS acceptance devices; (vi) information exchange on the current ATM and payment terminal ecosystem. Call for candidates closed 10/04/2026; workstreams began May 2026. The most recent published RDG outcome (29th meeting, held 28/04/2026, published 28/07/2026) records only that the RDG 'took note of the update and proposed workplans' for G5 and B1 and that an overview of workstream sprint timelines plus the list of selected G5/B1 participants 'will be prepared for the next RDG'. NO G5 specification, deliverable or date has been published as at 27/08/2026.
signals.source_name: ECB, 'Update on the work of the digital euro scheme's Rulebook Development Group' — sixth progress report (§4.2) + ECB, 29th RDG Meeting Outcome
signals.implies: G5 is where Printec's entire euro-area ATM and POS estate gets specified, and NCR Atleos / Verifone / Castles are the vendor classes G5 explicitly calls out ('ATM and terminal providers'). Point (iii) is the sharpest: the ECB is assessing whether offline digital euro can be pushed into ALREADY-CERTIFIED POS and ATM infrastructure — if yes, this is a firmware/kernel refresh across the installed base (x-core, TMS pushes); if no, it is a forklift replacement cycle. Point (iv) drags PCI/Thales HSM and physical ATM security into scope. Printec should be seeking sight of the G5 workplan through NCR Atleos and through the Greek/Croatian/Cypriot bank participants, not waiting for publication.
signals.likelihood: Medium — a first G5 output or participant list is plausible at the 30th RDG / in the next RDG progress report within 6 months
signals.followup: Watch https://www.ecb.europa.eu/euro/digital_euro/timeline/profuse/html/index.en.html for the 30th RDG Outcome and the next RDG progress report — the G5 participant list will name which vendors and banks are in the room. Ask NCR Atleos directly whether it or ATMIA has a G5 seat.

signals.entity: ECB / ECPC (CPACE), nexo standards, Berlin Group — front-end standards for digital euro
signals.country: Euro area — GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, AT, BG
signals.signal: The ECB signed cooperation agreements in April 2026 with three European standardisation bodies to reuse their open standards for digital euro front-end processing: CPACE (contactless tap-to-pay over NFC between payment device and payment terminal), NEXO standards (balance updates and reconciliation for online POS, e-commerce, m-commerce AND 'ATM digital euro payments'), and Berlin Group (alias-based use cases and balance enquiry). The ECB's 16/07/2026 ERPB deck states these standards 'are usable immediately and will become MANDATORY once the legislation is adopted', and positions them explicitly against 'MasterCard, Visa and other schemes closed protocols'. ECB representatives now sit in the standardisation bodies' governing bodies and working groups (ECPC Technical Working Group, Berlin Group OpenFinance Task Force). [Acronyms: CPACE = Common implementation Project for A Common European contactless protocol; nexo = European card-acceptance messaging standards body; NFC = near-field communication.]
signals.source_name: ECB, 'ECB collaborates with European standard setters to facilitate digital euro payments', ERPB 20th general technical session, Agenda item 2 (published 30/07/2026, presentation dated 16/07/2026)
signals.implies: This is the single most concrete terminal-estate obligation in the workstream: once the Regulation is adopted, CPACE (terminal kernel) and nexo (acquirer/terminal messaging, ATM included) become MANDATORY, not optional. For Printec that is a Verifone/Castles kernel + TMS mass-deployment programme across every acquiring customer, and a nexo interface project on the NCR/x-core ATM side. Banks that already run nexo-conformant acquiring are cheap to upgrade; those on proprietary/scheme-only protocols are the net-new contest. Budget commitment: 6-12 months ahead of the Regulation's application, i.e. the conversation to open with acquirers in Q4-2026/H1-2027 as trilogue conclusion nears.
signals.likelihood: High that CPACE/nexo remain the selected standards; timing bound to the Regulation, not to a fixed date
signals.followup: Confirm with Verifone and Castles their CPACE kernel certification roadmap and with NCR Atleos the nexo/ATM position; check whether Printec's TMS can push a CPACE kernel to the installed base without a site visit — that is the margin question.

signals.signal: A fourth standardisation agreement, with the EPC, is being formalised through a Memorandum of Understanding; the ECB states 'the process for approving the MoU by the ECB decision-making bodies was initiated at the end of June 2026'. The candidate EPC standards named are the QR-code payment standard EPC024-22 — cited for online POS, e-commerce, m-commerce 'and, potentially, ATM transactions using QR codes' — and Verification of Payee (VoP), whose reuse is under technical investigation. [VoP = Verification of Payee, the payee-name-versus-IBAN check.]
signals.source_name: ECB, RDG sixth progress report (§4.1) and ERPB digital euro standards presentation
signals.implies: EPC024-22 QR at the ATM is the second initiation route already written into rulebook Annex D1 #4 alongside card. If the MoU lands, QR becomes a formal digital euro acceptance channel — meaning ATMs in the footprint need a QR scanner or an on-screen dynamic-QR capability, and POS terminals a QR path. For Printec this is a fascia/peripheral question on the NCR estate (many installed machines have no scanner) and a software question on newer ones. It also links the digital euro to the VoP work already funded for 09/07/2027 in CZ/HU/RO — potential reuse of the same VoP component.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that the MoU is signed within 6 months
signals.followup: Watch for an ECB press release announcing the EPC MoU; then check whether EPC024-22 is referenced normatively in the next rulebook version's ATM section. Survey the installed NCR base in GR/CY/HR for QR-scanner capability.

signals.entity: ECB digital euro pilot — 36 PSPs, 19 NCBs
signals.country: GR, HR, CY, AT, SI, SK (in footprint); BG excluded
signals.signal: The pilot will validate FOUR use cases only: (1) online P2P via user alias or DEAN, (2) OFFLINE P2P via NFC device-to-device, (3) online P2B at the point of sale via NFC where the merchant is equipped with a SOFTPOS application on their own device, (4) online P2B in e-commerce/m-commerce. There is NO ATM use case and NO physical/hardware POS terminal use case; acquiring PSPs 'may be asked to offer a SoftPOS solution and/or an e-commerce/m-commerce solution'. B2P refunds are inside the P2B scope, not a fifth use case. Timeline confirmed: call opened 05/03/2026, closed 14/05/2026; selection notified end-June 2026; PSP participation agreements signed July 2026; PILOT DEVELOPMENT PHASE STARTED Q3-2026 (now) covering development, DESP onboarding/integration, user testing and BACK-END CERTIFICATION; operational phase H2-2027 for 12 months, completing H2-2028, with the contracting NCB able to extend by up to six months at its discretion. Pilot PSPs may not charge end users any fee. The 19 participating NCBs are Belgium, Germany, Estonia, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Croatia, Italy, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Austria, Portugal, Slovenia, Slovakia and Finland — BULGARIA IS NOT AMONG THEM, despite the BNB having joined the Eurosystem on 01/01/2026. A merchant call for expression of interest is still to be launched to cover the two P2B use cases.
signals.source_name: ECB, 'FAQs on the digital euro pilot' (updated 14/07/2026) + ECB press release 'ECB selects 36 payment service providers to join digital euro pilot' + ERPB Agenda item 3 'Pilot update'
signals.implies: TWO consequences for Printec. (a) THREAT: the Eurosystem's own reference acceptance model for in-store digital euro is SoftPOS on the merchant's phone, not a Verifone/Castles terminal — an explicit softening of the hardware-POS lane that Printec must answer with a SoftPOS/TMS story rather than ignore. (b) OPPORTUNITY, near-term and small: pilot PSPs in Greece, Croatia, Cyprus, Austria, Slovenia and Slovakia are IN DEVELOPMENT NOW (Q3-2026) and face DESP integration, user testing and back-end certification with no fee income — integration and testing services, transaction monitoring (INETCO) and fraud tooling around the beta digital euro are billable to those PSPs in the next two quarters. Budget commitment for pilot PSPs is already committed; for the merchant-acceptance wave it follows the merchant call. Bulgaria's absence means the Bulgarian estate gets no pilot-driven work at all — BG spend stays on the euro-changeover and instant-payments track.
signals.likelihood: High — development phase is live now; merchant call likely within 6 months
signals.followup: Identify WHICH Greek, Croatian and Cypriot PSPs are among the 36 (PSPs are permitted to self-announce under the ECB communication guidelines — check Alpha Bank, Piraeus, NBG, Eurobank, Erste Croatia, Bank of Cyprus press pages). Watch for the merchant call for expression of interest. Ask BNB why Bulgaria is absent and whether it will join a later wave.

signals.entity: European Parliament / Council of the EU — Digital Euro Regulation (2023/0212(COD))
signals.country: EU / euro area; plus CZ, HU, RO via the companion non-euro-PSP file
signals.signal: ECON adopted its position on the single currency package on 23/06/2026 (digital euro file: 43 in favour, 14 against, 1 abstention). On 09/07/2026 plenary confirmed the negotiating mandate by 416 votes to 169 with 22 abstentions after PfE, ECR and ESN challenged it; the companion file on digital euro services by PSPs incorporated in NON-EURO member states was approved by show of hands, and the third file on legal tender of cash was not contested. Rapporteur Fernando Navarrete Rojas (EPP, ES). Negotiations opened with the IRISH Presidency. Parliament's mandate specifies: most businesses must ACCEPT the digital euro (exemptions for self-employed and small/micro enterprises that accept no other digital payment; temporary refusal allowed e.g. during a power outage); basic services free of charge; merchant and inter-PSP fees capped and offline payments entirely fee-free; a cap on individual holdings whose EU ceiling would be SET BY THE COMMISSION on ECB recommendation and reviewed at least every two years — NO euro figure is fixed in the mandate itself; businesses may not hold digital euro except to accumulate incoming payments for up to 24 hours; the digital euro bears no interest; and, once authorised, A ROLL-OUT PERIOD OF AT LEAST 24 MONTHS would follow to give banks, providers and users time to prepare. MEPs also require the ECB to finalise the rulebook, build the infrastructure and run real-life pilot tests before launch. The Council's general approach dates from 19/12/2025. Trilogue dates themselves are reported only in press/law-firm commentary (first political trilogue 13/07/2026, further rounds after the summer recess, target political agreement before end-2026) — treat the 13/07/2026 date as PRESS-TIER, not confirmed by an EP or Council primary source.
signals.source_name: European Parliament press releases 'Digital euro: MEPs ready to start negotiations' (09/07/2026) and 'Digital euro: MEPs want to ensure sovereignty, privacy and financial stability' (23/06/2026)
signals.implies: The 'at least 24 months' roll-out period is the budget-planning anchor Printec should be using with banks instead of any 2029 date: political agreement targeted end-2026 → adoption 2027 → acceptance and distribution obligations bite ~24 months later. Mandatory merchant acceptance drives the terminal-estate refresh (Verifone/Castles + TMS + CPACE kernel); mandatory free basic services and capped fees squeeze PSP economics and therefore favour Printec's managed-service and multivendor (x-core) cost-out pitch over bank-built solutions. The separate non-euro-PSP file is the reason Czech, Hungarian and Romanian banks (CSOB, Komercni, OTP, MBH, BCR, BT, Raiffeisen) are in scope at all — they would be permitted to distribute the digital euro. IMPORTANT: do NOT quote any holding-limit euro figure to customers; neither co-legislator mandate contains one.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that a political agreement is reached before end-2026 as targeted
signals.followup: Track the Council press room and EP Legislative Observatory (procedure 2023/0212(COD)) for a confirmed trilogue calendar and for the provisional political agreement text; the number that matters commercially is the final roll-out period, not the holding limit. Consilium timeline page was 403-blocked this run — retry.

signals.entity: European Parliament / Council — Regulation on the legal tender of euro banknotes and coins (2023/0208(COD))
signals.country: Euro area — GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, AT, BG
signals.signal: The third file of the single currency package entered trilogue UNCONTESTED on 09/07/2026 (ECON position adopted 46 votes to 4, 8 abstentions, rapporteur Navarrete). Substance: Member States must designate national competent authorities with oversight and regulatory powers over cash ACCEPTANCE and ACCESS, and must submit an ANNUAL REPORT to the Commission and the ECB assessing both. That assessment rests on a COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING ACT defining common indicators — the file explicitly names 'density of cash access points in relation to the population' as an access indicator and 'level of ex ante unilateral exclusions of payments in cash' as an acceptance indicator. Where the assessment is negative, the Member State must set out remedial policy measures such as prohibiting cash exclusions or imposing GEOGRAPHICAL ACCESS REQUIREMENTS; if it fails to act, the COMMISSION IS EMPOWERED TO ADOPT IMPLEMENTING ACTS IMPOSING COUNTRY-SPECIFIC MEASURES. The Council's December-2025 position additionally requires RESILIENCE MEASURES ensuring continuity of cash payments during major disruptions to electronic payment systems. Parliament's plenary line on 09/07/2026 confirms: euro area countries obliged to keep cash accessible, businesses not allowed to ban cash, regular monitoring with special attention to the elderly, low-income individuals and the unbanked.
signals.source_name: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule, 'Scope and effects of legal tender of euro banknotes and coins' (2023/0208(COD)) + EP plenary press release 09/07/2026
signals.implies: THE BIGGEST ATM SIGNAL IN THIS WORKSTREAM, and it sits in the cash file rather than the digital euro file. An EU-wide, Commission-enforced ATM/cash-access-point DENSITY metric is the same mechanism as Slovenia's draft 60-ATM/100k floor and Hungary's Act XVIII of 2025 rural-ATM mandate, but applied across the whole euro area with a Commission backstop. Affected: every euro-area bank in the footprint — Alpha Bank, Eurobank, NBG, Piraeus (GR), Bank of Cyprus, Hellenic (CY), Erste/PBZ/Zagrebacka (HR), NLB/Nova KBM (SI), Slovenska sporitelna/VUB/Tatra (SK), Erste/RBI/BAWAG (AT), and now Bulgarian banks post-euro. What they must buy: additional ATM estate in thin-density areas (NCR dispense and recycling), cash automation/recyclers to make marginal sites economic, NCR APTRA OptiCash cash optimisation to hold CIT cost down while the estate grows, telemetry/monitoring for uptime evidence, and — from the Council's resilience clause — offline-capable cash dispensing during electronic outages. WHEN TO COMMIT BUDGET: the obligation lands via the Commission implementing act defining the indicators, which follows adoption; banks should be scoping estate-density gap analyses 6-12 months ahead, i.e. from H1-2027, and Printec should be selling that gap analysis NOW as a pre-sales instrument.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High — the file is uncontested and moves with the package toward end-2026 political agreement
signals.followup: Obtain the consolidated ECON report text for 2023/0208(COD) and check whether the density indicator survives in the mandate articles (not just the explanatory train entry). Cross-read against the Slovenian post-consultation draft (17/08/2026 close) and MNB Reg 19/2025 — national mandates that already exceed this will be the first spend.

signals.entity: ECB / Euro Retail Payments Board (ERPB) — 'Fit in the ecosystem' workstream
signals.country: Euro area — GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, AT, BG
signals.signal: The 20th ERPB general technical session on the digital euro was published on 30/07/2026 (session held 16/07/2026). Next steps announced: the ECB project team will finalise a structured proposal for follow-up analyses arising from the 30 June 2026 ABI Lab cost/simplification workshop, with the topical split between RDG and ERPB to be communicated to the market; and it will 'kickstart collaborative work on MAPPING OUT THE DIGITAL EURO ROLLOUT STRATEGY', to be structured as a collective discussion at the 21ST ERPB GENERAL TECHNICAL SESSION ON THE DIGITAL EURO, SCHEDULED FOR 13 OCTOBER 2026. Areas flagged for future technical analysis include 'Offline: payment acceptance and readiness requirements', account switching, and multiple accounts & holding limits; areas flagged for reuse include notifications, regulatory reporting and transaction lists; for optimisation, balance management/'mirror accounts' and reuse of card-issuing capabilities. A co-badging deep-dive (April 2026) concluded co-badging is a VOLUNTARY opportunity that could give domestic card schemes pan-euro-area reach, subject to legal provisions (e.g. interplay with the Interchange Fee Regulation).
signals.source_name: ECB, 'Fit in the Ecosystem — stocktake and next steps', ERPB 20th general technical session, Agenda item 4
signals.implies: 13/10/2026 is the next hard, dated event in this workstream and the first time the ECB will discuss a ROLLOUT STRATEGY with the market — the document that will eventually contain the acceptance-readiness dates Printec's customers need for budgeting. 'Offline: payment acceptance and readiness requirements' being on the future-analysis list is the thread that eventually reaches the ATM and terminal estate (offline acceptance needs secure elements, HSM key management — Thales lane). Co-badging matters commercially: if domestic schemes co-badge with the digital euro, the terminal kernel and TMS work is combined rather than duplicated, which is a single funded project rather than two.
signals.followup: Retrieve the 21st ERPB general technical session documents after 13/10/2026 — specifically any rollout-strategy paper and whether it carries acceptance-readiness dates for terminals and ATMs.

signals.entity: Czech National Bank (CNB / Ceska narodni banka)
signals.signal: [STANDING — dated 2025] The CNB's own CBDC page states that the CNB Bank Board 'has so far taken no decision on the possible issuance of a Czech CBDC' ('Bankovni rada CNB dosud neprijala zadne rozhodnuti ve veci pripadne emise ceskych CBDC') and that 'a necessary precondition for the CNB to issue a CBDC would be a corresponding change of legislation, since the existing legal framework does not permit CBDC issuance in the Czech Republic' ('stavajici pravni uprava emisi CBDC v CR neumoznuje'). A CBDC working group has existed since February 2021. The most recent item listed on the page is a 06/09/2025 commentary by J. Kubicek, 'Digitalni euro jako penezenka budoucnosti?' [The digital euro as the wallet of the future?]. No pilot, no date, no legal basis.
signals.source_name: Ceska narodni banka, 'Digitalni penize centralnich bank (CBDC)' [Central bank digital money (CBDC)] — CNB official site, Czech-language page
signals.implies: Negative signal, and a useful one: there is NO CBDC-driven ATM or terminal spend trigger in the Czech Republic, and none can arise without primary legislation. Czech bank spend in Printec's lanes remains driven by the 09/01/2027 receive / 09/07/2027 send-and-VoP instant-euro obligations under Reg (EU) 2024/886, not by a digital koruna. Czech banks WOULD however be in scope of the companion EU file allowing non-euro-area PSPs to distribute the digital euro.
signals.likelihood: Low that any CZ CBDC step occurs in 6-12 months
signals.followup: Re-check the CNB page and the CNB Lab 'Digital Assets' / 'Pilot Payments' streams once a year; the trigger to watch is a legislative amendment, not a CNB statement.

signals.entity: National Bank of Serbia (NBS / Narodna banka Srbije) — digital dinar
signals.signal: [STANDING — dated 2025] The Law on Amendments to the Law on the National Bank of Serbia (Zakon o izmenama i dopunama Zakona o Narodnoj banci Srbije), published in the Official Gazette of the Republic of Serbia No. 19/2025, inserted into Article 53 a provision giving the NBS the EXCLUSIVE RIGHT to issue dinars in digital form (digitalni dinar), 'in accordance with regulations that may be adopted by the Executive Board'. The same amendments give the NBS power to license and supervise virtual-currency service providers. As at 27/08/2026 no Executive Board regulation implementing the digital dinar, no pilot and no target date has been identified. Serbia's own commentary frames the digital euro pilot as the likely influence on domestic timing.
signals.source_name: Zakon o izmenama i dopunama Zakona o Narodnoj banci Srbije, 'Sl. glasnik RS', br. 19/2025 [Law amending the Law on the National Bank of Serbia, Official Gazette of the RS No. 19/2025] — consolidated text via Paragraf legal database
signals.implies: Serbia now has the LEGAL BASIS for a CBDC that the Czech Republic lacks, but no implementing act — so still no spend trigger. For Printec (Raiffeisen Serbia x-core, AikBank NCR recyclers) the practical read is that any digital dinar would follow, not lead, the digital euro, and would reuse whatever ATM/terminal specification the ECB's G5 workstream produces. Worth a watching brief only. Note this row's source is a legal-database reproduction, not the NBS site or the gazette PDF directly — verify before quoting to a customer.
signals.likelihood: Low that an NBS Executive Board digital dinar regulation appears within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Re-verify the Article 53 wording against the NBS 'Zakoni' page (https://www.nbs.rs/sr/drugi-nivo-navigacije/propisi/zakoni/) or the Sluzbeni glasnik PDF, and check NBS Executive Board decisions for any digital dinar implementing act.

signals.signal: [STANDING] The NBU's own e-hryvnia page (fetched 27/08/2026 with a desktop User-Agent after the standard fetch route) still describes the project in options-analysis terms: the NBU 'is considering and processing the following possible options for using the e-hryvnia that will shape its design and main features' — retail non-cash payments with programmable targeted money, e-hryvnia in virtual-asset circulation, and cross-border payments. The e-hryvnia is defined in the Law of Ukraine On Payment Services and 'if the decision to introduce the e-hryvnia is approved, it will be legal tender'. Design features under study include DLT-based wallet-access recovery and OFFLINE PAYMENTS including the case where neither payer nor payee has connectivity. The project dates to September 2021; the page carries no pilot date, no decision date and no issuance date. Published NBU materials remain the pilot analytical report and the CBDCinUA conference report; nothing new was found in 2026 NBU news.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine, 'E-hryvnia' (official NBU site, English)
signals.implies: No CBDC spend trigger in Ukraine. Ukrainian bank spend in Printec's lanes (PrivatBank NCR recyclers) remains driven by the NBU Board Resolution No.143 information-security deadline of 13/12/2026 and by banknote/validator work, not by the e-hryvnia. The one forward-looking hook worth noting is that the NBU's stated design target includes fully offline payments — which, if ever built, would land on the same secure-element/HSM ground as the euro-area offline digital euro.
signals.likelihood: Low — NBU has repeatedly said CBDC investment is not a wartime priority
signals.followup: Re-check bank.gov.ua/en/payments/e-hryvnia and NBU news quarterly; a Board decision or a named pilot partner would be the first real change since 2021.

coverage_notes: Fresh run (no checkpoint file existed for 27/08/2026). Primary-source-first: worked the ECB digital euro 'Technical documents and research' document register (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/euro/digital_euro/timeline/profuse/html/index.en.html), which the baseline had not walked, and downloaded/extracted the underlying PDFs locally with pdfminer rather than relying on the fetch tool (the ECB PDFs return compressed streams the fetch tool cannot read). Documents opened in full: RDG sixth progress report (06/07/2026), 29th RDG Meeting Outcome (published 28/07/2026), rulebook v0.91 Annex D1 #4 Acceptance device (the ATM chapter), PSP Participation Agreement Appendix 2.G Pilot Timeline, and all three substantive ERPB 20th-general-technical-session decks published 30/07/2026 (standards, pilot update, fit-in-the-ecosystem). Also read the ECB pilot FAQ (updated 14/07/2026) and press release of 14/07/2026 in full, and both EP press releases (23/06/2026 ECON, 09/07/2026 plenary) plus the EP Legislative Train entry for the legal-tender-of-cash file. FOUR BRIEFED QUESTIONS ANSWERED: (1) NO rulebook version after v0.91 exists as at 27/08/2026 — sections 8, 9 and Annex F1 are still placeholders due in H2-2026. (2) G5 has a mandate and a workplan but NO published output; the latest RDG outcome only records that the workplan and the participant list will be tabled at the next RDG. (3) The 19-NCB / 36-PSP pilot has moved into its development phase (Q3-2026) and now has a confirmed NCB list — Greece, Croatia, Cyprus, Austria, Slovenia and Slovakia are in, BULGARIA IS NOT, despite BNB Eurosystem membership from 01/01/2026. (4) The EU legislative step is real and dated: ECON 23/06/2026, EP plenary mandate 09/07/2026 by 416/169/22, trilogue with the Irish Presidency. The unsupported holding-limit figure was NOT repeated — the EP mandate delegates the ceiling to the Commission with a two-yearly review and fixes no euro figure, which is stated explicitly in the relevant row. The most commercially important discovery this run is that the ATM driver sits in the THIRD file of the single currency package (legal tender of euro banknotes and coins), which carries a Commission-defined 'density of cash access points' indicator and a Commission power to impose country-specific implementing acts — an EU-wide analogue of the Slovenian and Hungarian ATM mandates. GENUINE GAPS: (a) the identity of the individual Greek, Croatian and Cypriot PSPs among the 36 is not published by the ECB and was not established this run — PSPs are permitted to self-announce, so their own press pages are the route; (b) the G5 participant list is not yet published; (c) Hungary's MNB CBDC position could not be confirmed against an MNB primary page within this run's budget (only secondary Hungarian fintech press was found, which is not good enough to report — deliberately omitted rather than reported weakly); (d) trilogue meeting dates exist only in law-firm and payments-association commentary and are flagged as press-tier in the row rather than asserted; (e) no Governing Council decision on the digital euro has been taken or is due — the ECB has stated repeatedly that it will only decide on issuance once the Regulation is adopted, so the absence of a Governing Council step is a finding, not a coverage gap. Searched but found nothing new dated AFTER 02/08/2026 in this workstream: the ECB published nothing on the digital euro in August 2026 (the register's most recent entries are 30/07/2026), which is consistent with the EU institutional summer recess.
